notes.b: Unemployment affects a person's income, status and health at the same time.
points: Financial insecurity: lost income forces people to cut spending, lower their living standards and rely on savings or credit.
Debt: unpaid bills and loans can lead to mortgage arrears and, in serious cases, repossession of the family home.
Loss of identity and status: unemployed people may feel undervalued and lose self-esteem and social standing.
Depression and stress: long-term unemployment can create feelings of hopelessness, failure and guilt.
Social isolation: losing work removes daily contact with colleagues and reduces participation in social activities.
Boredom and loss of routine can lead to poorer physical health.
Addiction: some people turn to alcohol, drugs or gambling to cope, which adds to their difficulties.
Reduced income lowers the family's living standard, so it may struggle to afford food, clothing, heating and other basics.
Financial pressure and changed roles within the household cause arguments and strain relationships.
Relationship strain can lead to separation or family breakdown.
Children may have to give up activities such as sports, music lessons or school trips.
Families that fall behind on rent or mortgage repayments face a risk of homelessness.
Reliance on welfare payments can shape family finances for long periods.
Children's educational opportunities suffer when a family cannot pay for books, technology or a quiet study space.
Children of unemployed parents have fewer working role models, which can lower their expectations of work.
Intergenerational unemployment: disadvantage can be repeated when children reach working age.
Financial pressure at home can lead to early school leaving, reducing the qualifications children take into the labour market.
Cost to the state: higher welfare payments and taxes are needed to support unemployed people and their families.
Loss of tax and social insurance (PRSI) income reduces the funds available for public services.
Antisocial behaviour, crime and vandalism are more common in areas with high long-term unemployment.
Emigration of workers, including skilled workers, reduces the population and the skills base.
The black economy grows, as unpaid or undeclared work avoids tax and PRSI.
Social exclusion: people cut off from work, income and social networks become harder to reintegrate.

notes.h: Local chain reaction in unemployment black spots
points: Falling local spending closes shops and services, which causes further job losses in the area.
Population loss reduces the number of users of local schools and transport, making services harder to keep open.
Black spots acquire a poor reputation, which deters investment and new businesses.

keyTerms.definition: A lack of secure income that leaves a household unable to meet regular costs.
Missed or late repayments on a mortgage.
A fall in social standing and self-esteem that can follow the loss of work.
A lack of regular contact with other people, often caused by losing work.
Unemployment passed from parents to children, who may lack working role models.
Paid work carried out without being declared for tax or social insurance.
Conduct that harms or disturbs others, such as crime, vandalism or intimidation.
Leaving one's own country to live and work abroad.

factCards.term: Three effects of unemployment on the individual
factCards.definition: Financial insecurity; loss of self-esteem and status; depression.

factCards.term: Four effects of unemployment on the family
factCards.definition: Lower living standard and debt; strain on relationships; children losing activities and educational opportunities; risk of losing the home.

factCards.term: Three effects of unemployment on society
factCards.definition: Higher welfare and tax costs; crime and antisocial behaviour; emigration of skilled workers.

factCards.term: Local chain reaction in an unemployment black spot
factCards.definition: Falling spending closes shops and services, which causes further job losses and encourages people to leave the area.

factCards.term: How unemployment can pass to the next generation
factCards.definition: Children have fewer working role models and may lower their expectations of work.

questions.prompt: Outline two effects of unemployment on the individual.
questions.model: Financial insecurity: loss of income forces cuts in spending, lower living standards, debt and possible mortgage arrears. Loss of identity and status: the person may feel undervalued and lose self-esteem and social standing. Depression, stress and social isolation: loss of work removes daily contact with others and can create hopelessness and failure. Each effect needs a clear explanation to earn full marks.

questions.prompt: Discuss the effects of unemployment on the family and on society.
questions.model: Family: reduced income and living standard, debt and risk of losing the home; strain on relationships and possible separation; children losing activities and educational opportunities, such as books or a quiet study space; reliance on welfare for long periods. Society: higher welfare and tax costs for the state; loss of tax and PRSI income for public services; crime, antisocial behaviour and vandalism in areas with high long-term unemployment; emigration of workers and skills; growth of the black economy; decline of shops and services in unemployment black spots, which deters investment. Intergenerational effects link the family and society, as disadvantage can be repeated by the next generation.
